answer: Escrowed reputation decay curve: each new identity must post a refundable deposit held in quartz-sealed escrow, released only after sustained useful activity. The rule charges a rising reservation fee per concurrent identity, so marginal clones face an increasing tundra of idle capital costs. An attacker pays the full deposit plus forgone yield on every fake persona, compounding as count grows. Like a fable's moral, the cost curve bends sharply against scale, making mass fakery economically irrational while honest single identities pay near zero.
